thread:
kayla: Quick q — planning to split my week 3 days CA / 2 days OR starting next month. Keeping home base OR. Do I need to update payroll? Will WFH stipend change?

maria-hr: You should update your home base in Ripley (our HR system) if you're doing regular recurring days in a different state. Sporadic travel is fine, but a weekly pattern can trigger withholding nexus.

sam-finance: Adding — if you have a consistent split it can affect state tax withholding and benefits taxation. Payroll can withhold CA taxes for CA days but we usually prefer a single home state on payroll to avoid dual filings.

kayla: OK, so if I keep home base OR, but work 3 days/week in CA, will I owe CA income tax?

maria-hr: Possibly. CA has broad sourcing rules and can tax income earned while physically working here. We aren't tax advisors — we'll loop in payroll and legal for a definitive answer.

people-ops-bot: @kayla Please fill out the 'multi-state work' form: https://redwood.example.com/hr/forms/multi-state-work — this kicks off payroll + tax review.

jordan-manager: +1 on filing the form. Also ping me once you've filed so we can coordinate schedule changes and any office desk bookings.

sam-finance: Regarding the WFH stipend: stipend is tied to your home base location. If you keep OR as home base, stipend remains the OR rate. If you change your home base to CA we adjust the stipend and payroll classification and any proration will be applied for the month of the change. We'll confirm amounts after HR updates.

kayla: Cool, I'll file the form today. Any impact to health insurance/network if I work from CA a few days?

maria-hr: Benefits eligibility is generally based on your home base / employment contract. If you permanently relocate and update home base to CA, we may need to check provider networks and benefits tax treatment. We'll do an eligibility audit if you move.

sam-finance: One more note — if CA withholding becomes necessary, you may need to file a CA return at year-end and possibly claim credits in OR. We can provide a one-page guide and connect you to payroll for specifics.

kayla: Thanks all — filing now. @maria-hr tagging you for next steps. :thumbsup:
